title: SOV Schematic Run Receipt
description: Documentation only: receipts are built by runReceipt in src/07-state-space.js. The one receipt every run operation returns on every surface (browser API, HTTP, MCP): schematic.run.start, .step, .settle, .trace, schematic.state.query, schematic.run.replay and schematic.run.drop (STATE-SPACE.md, Surfaces). A drop's receipt is the dropped run as it stood, with result null. Running never changes the document, its revision, history or recovery. The HTTP status is the only surface-specific field and is not part of the receipt. Runs are addressed by handle.

runId.description: the run's content-derived id (the first 12 hex digits of its replay key's hash; record ids carry it); two starts with the same replay key share it. Null when no run was found or started

handle.description: the address of the run on this surface: the run id, a '.', and the surface registry's start counter from 1 (e.g. dd38fae2158e.3). Every start gets a new handle, so a second start with the same replay key never touches the first run; step, settle, trace and state.query take it. Null for a replay (not registered), a refusal with no run, and a receipt built outside a registry

tickBefore.description: the run's last processed tick before the operation (null before any, and for start and replay)

tickAfter.description: the run's last processed tick after the operation

head.description: the hash of the run's last ledger entry after the operation, which a truncated trace cannot match

result.description: null on a refusal. start: the start ledger entry's body {replayKey, budget}; step: {tick, records}; settle: {kind: quiet} | {kind: oscillating, period, subjects} | {kind: budget, left}; trace: the trace (trace@0.1); state.query: the matching state records, in record order; replay: {records}; drop: null

code.description: RUN_NOT_FOUND (unknown handle; HTTP 404), RUN_LIMIT (a start on a surface already holding 64 runs; HTTP 409; nothing is evicted), INPUT_INVALID (including a surface budget over 1000000, and over HTTP a body that is not JSON or a path that does not decode, both HTTP 400), PACK_INVALID, QUERY_INVALID, RUN_INVALID, RUN_REFUSED, MERGE_FORM, BUDGET_SPENT (step), TRACE_INVALID, REPLAY_KEY_MISMATCH or REPLAY_DIVERGED

details.description: what the refusal names besides its code and message, the same on every surface: {refusals} for RUN_REFUSED and a PACK_INVALID from packs that do not load; {tick, left} for BUDGET_SPENT; {fields} for REPLAY_KEY_MISMATCH; {entry, errors} for TRACE_INVALID; {tick}, {entry} or {record} for REPLAY_DIVERGED; {subject} for MERGE_FORM; {definitions} for PACK_INVALID 'this page carries no packs'. Absent when the refusal names nothing more
